# Triage: `pub` items with no consumer outside their own file

*Generated by `scripts/scan-pub-item-usage.py --triage`. Do not hand-edit.*

Regenerate with:

```bash
python3 scripts/scan-pub-item-usage.py --triage \
  --external-tree /path/to/api-consumer > scripts/pub-item-triage.md
```

**This table was generated without the external-tree cross-check, so its
`keep` column is wrong. Regenerate it with `--external-tree` before acting
on anything here.**

## Verdicts

| Verdict | Meaning | Tests-only | All |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `keep` | Live through a consumer `pub(crate)` would not reach: an integration test that compiles as its own crate, the out-of-tree tree, serde/schemars, or a reason recorded in scripts/pub-item-verdicts.json. | 447 | 734 |
| `narrow` | Used inside its own file. Wrong visibility, not dead code. Narrowing to `pub(crate)` shrinks the public surface and lets `dead_code` police it from then on. | 16 | 1327 |
| `wire-or-delete` | No consumer anywhere and no in-file use. Give it a production call site or remove it. | 0 | 80 |

Tests-only total: **463**. Full candidate list: **2141**.

`narrow` is the highest-leverage verdict and should be preferred over deletion
wherever it applies. It converts an item rustc cannot see into one it polices for
free, so the same item can never rot silently a second time.

## Tests-only items

The slice with the highest density of real findings and the lowest risk of a
false positive, so it is where the cleanup starts. A symbol whose only consumer
is its own test suite is not shipping behaviour.

There is no leave message anywhere on the wire (GossipMsg carries Heartbeat, Join, Ping, Ack, PingReq, IndirectAck; MeshMessage carries MembershipUpdate, Ping, Pong) and no shutdown path sends one, so a node that exits cleanly is evicted by the failure detector under probe_timeout or dead_timeout like any corpse. Building it is a wire change plus a lifecycle hook, not a bug fix. The constant is kept so the label value stays reserved, and the doc comments that used to promise a LeaveRequest handler now say it does not exist. |

### sbproxy-transport

| Item | Location | Verdict | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pub fn decode_all_raw` | `crates/sbproxy-transport/src/grpc/frame.rs:113` | `keep` | Answered on WOR-2225: the strict decoder is correct where it is called, and this one is not dead code so much as code for a direction that is not wired yet. grpc/web.rs:80 is the request path, and gRPC-Web only folds trailers into the body because a browser cannot read them off a response; a request has no trailers to fold, since gRPC carries none in that direction at all. So decode_all rejecting 0x80 there is the spec-correct behaviour, and it errors rather than misparsing. This walker is the response-direction counterpart, which the proxy does not need while it is the gRPC-Web server rather than a client of one. Tests now pin the split in both directions so the question does not get reopened. |
